From 123a9e7d83213bcc0478840bab2270113275fb0a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Christopher Faulet <cfaulet@haproxy.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Dec 2023 10:27:53 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] BUG/MAJOR: stconn: Disable zero-copy forwarding if consumer
 is shut or in error

A regression was introduced by commit 2421c6fa7d ("BUG/MEDIUM: stconn: Block
zero-copy forwarding if EOS/ERROR on consumer side"). When zero-copy
forwarding is inuse and the consumer side is shut or in error, we declare it
as blocked and it is woken up. The idea is to handle this state at the
stream-connector level. However this definitly blocks receives on the
producer side. So if the mux is unable to close by itself, but instead wait
the peer to shut, this can lead to a wake up loop. And indeed, with the
passthrough multiplexer this may happen.

To fix the issue and prevent any loop, instead of blocking the zero-copy
forwarding, we now disable it. This way, the stream-connector on producer
side will fallback on classical receives and will be able to handle peer
shutdown properly. In addition, the wakeup of the consumer side was
removed. This will be handled, if necessary, by sc_notify().

This patch should fix the issue #2395. It must be backported to 2.9.

diff --git a/include/haproxy/stconn.h b/include/haproxy/stconn.h
index 9b5502a7d..afab784ca 100644
--- a/include/haproxy/stconn.h
+++ b/include/haproxy/stconn.h
@@ -511,13 +511,9 @@ static inline size_t se_nego_ff(struct sedesc *se, struct buffer *input, size_t
 
 		se->iobuf.flags &= ~IOBUF_FL_FF_BLOCKED;
 		if (mux->nego_fastfwd && mux->done_fastfwd) {
-			/* Declare SE as blocked if EOS or an error was reported.
-			 * This may happen if fast-forward was scheduled before the I/O processing on <SC>.
-			 * Wake <SC> up in this case.
-			 */
+			/* Disable zero-copy forwarding if EOS or an error was reported. */
 			if (se_fl_test(se, SE_FL_EOS|SE_FL_ERROR|SE_FL_ERR_PENDING)) {
-				se->iobuf.flags |= IOBUF_FL_FF_BLOCKED;
-				tasklet_wakeup(se->sc->wait_event.tasklet);
+				se->iobuf.flags |= IOBUF_FL_NO_FF;
 				goto end;
 			}
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `include/haproxy/stconn.h`**
   - The code block that previously declared the stream endpoint (SE) as blocked when an End Of Stream (EOS) or an error was reported has been modified.
   - The lines that set the `IOBUF_FL_FF_BLOCKED` flag and woke up the stream connector (SC) tasklet have been removed.
   - Instead of blocking zero-copy forwarding, the code now sets the `IOBUF_FL_NO_FF` flag to disable zero-copy forwarding when EOS or an error is detected.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The changes in `stconn.h` address a regression introduced by a previous commit that incorrectly handled the state of zero-copy forwarding when the consumer side was shut or in error. 
- By disabling zero-copy forwarding instead of blocking it, the patch ensures that the producer side can revert to classical receiving methods, thus preventing potential wake-up loops that could occur with the passthrough multiplexer.
- The removal of the wake-up call for the consumer side indicates a shift in responsibility for handling the consumer's state, which will now be managed by the `sc_notify()` function if necessary, rather than directly in the zero-copy forwarding logic.

Here is the commit message:
BUG/MAJOR: stconn: Disable zero-copy forwarding if consumer
 is shut or in error

A regression was introduced by commit 2421c6fa7d ("BUG/MEDIUM: stconn: Block
zero-copy forwarding if EOS/ERROR on consumer side"). When zero-copy
forwarding is inuse and the consumer side is shut or in error, we declare it
as blocked and it is woken up. The idea is to handle this state at the
stream-connector level. However this definitly blocks receives on the
producer side. So if the mux is unable to close by itself, but instead wait
the peer to shut, this can lead to a wake up loop. And indeed, with the
passthrough multiplexer this may happen.

To fix the issue and prevent any loop, instead of blocking the zero-copy
forwarding, we now disable it. This way, the stream-connector on producer
side will fallback on classical receives and will be able to handle peer
shutdown properly. In addition, the wakeup of the consumer side was
removed. This will be handled, if necessary, by sc_notify().

This patch should fix the issue #2395. It must be backported to 2.9.

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the incorrect handling of zero-copy forwarding when the consumer side was shut or in an error state. The previous implementation blocked the zero-copy forwarding, which led to a wake-up loop on the producer side if the multiplexer could not close itself and was waiting for the peer to shut down. This created a situation where the producer could not properly handle the peer shutdown, resulting in a regression in functionality.

 		if (mux->nego_fastfwd && mux->done_fastfwd) {

-			 * Wake <SC> up in this case.

-				se->iobuf.flags |= IOBUF_FL_FF_BLOCKED;
-				tasklet_wakeup(se->sc->wait_event.tasklet);
+				se->iobuf.flags |= IOBUF_FL_NO_FF;
 				goto end;
 			}

The bug occurs because the previous implementation blocks zero-copy forwarding when the consumer side is shut or in an error state, which leads to a wake-up loop on the producer side. This happens because the producer is unable to handle the peer shutdown properly, as it is stuck in a loop trying to wake up the consumer side, which is already in a blocked state.

The code statements that fix the bug are:

Reason:
The fix disables zero-copy forwarding instead of blocking it when the consumer side is shut or in an error state. This allows the stream-connector on the producer side to fall back on classical receives, enabling it to handle the peer shutdown properly without entering a wake-up loop.
